title: Bounded Headroom Token Circuits with Priority Throttles for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Rina Patel
description: Introduce a deterministic, bounded headroom admission controller — the Token Circuit — that enforces throughput guarantees while enabling graceful overload shedding across priority lanes in Dedicated fleets. The controller combines a token-circuit admission window, per-tenant priority throttles, and a lightweight demotion path to protect SLO-bound tenants without causing system-wide tail latency spikes.
background: Current fleet admission logic relies on best-effort token buckets and coarse queue depth checks which lead to noisy neighbor effects under bursty ingress. We've seen P95/P99 latency cliffs when several tenants simultaneously enter bursting traffic patterns. Existing work (ratequeue admission and queued backpressure orchestrator) mitigates some cases but lacks a bounded headroom signal and an integrated demotion channel for lower-priority traffic. This ticket designs the Token Circuit pattern to fill that gap and provide cleaner autoscaler integration.
proposal: Design and implement a Token Circuit admission controller that enforces three guarantees: 1) Minimum reserved throughput per tenant (soft guaranteed), 2) Bounded queue headroom to limit memory and latency amplification, 3) Priority-aware shedding that demotes or rejects work from non-SLO tenants before impacting higher-tier customers. The controller exposes knobs for token refill cadence, headroom depth, demotion thresholds, and autoscaler feedback signals.
algorithm_details:
- Token Circuit: each tenant/fleet has a token balance that accrues at a configured reserved rate and can borrow up to a bounded headroom (H tokens) for short bursts. When balance <= 0 and headroom exhausted, admission is rejected or demoted based on priority.
- Priority Throttles: map customer tier -> lane (e.g., platinum/gold/silver/free). Higher lanes can borrow from a small shared emergency pool when overall fleet utilization < emergency_threshold.
- Demotion Path: accepted low-priority requests can be marked "demoted" and routed to a low-cost execution path (smaller batch sizes, lower GPU priority, or quantized replicas) or queued in a limited secondary queue with strict TTL.
- Autoscaler Hooks: the controller emits tension metrics (token_deficit_rate, sustained_headroom_utilization) consumed by autoscaler to drive scale-up decisions proactively and to relax headroom when capacity grows.
config_schema:
Configurable parameters (per-fleet or per-tenant):
- reserved_rate_tokens_per_sec (int)
- headroom_tokens (int)
- max_borrow_duration_ms (int)
- priority_lane (string)
- emergency_pool_tokens (int)
- demotion_ttl_ms (int)
- demotion_routes (list)
- autoscaler_tension_threshold (float)
- enforcement_mode (strict|soft|simulate)
rollout_plan: 1) Unit-tests + sim harness for synthetic burst scenarios (local). 2) Canary on internal staging fleets with enforcement_mode=simulate for 48h; collect token_deficit_rate and latency/sla signals. 3) Gradual canary to k=5 customer fleets with strict enforcement for low-risk tiers. 4) Expand to 20% fleets while monitoring cost and P99 tail. 5) Full rollout. Must include kill-switch route and per-fleet override via Console.
testing_and_metrics:
Key metrics to record:
- admitted_per_sec by tenant and lane
- token_deficit_rate (tokens/sec borrowed beyond reserved)
- headroom_exhaustion_events (count)
- demoted_request_rate
- rejected_request_rate
- P95/P99 latency by lane
- autoscaler_scale_events triggered_by_token_deficit
Acceptance criteria: no regression in Platinum P99 latency during canary; demotion events keep total memory usage < 70% of the pre-rollout peak in staged bursts.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Overly aggressive demotion could affect perceived quality for paid customers. Mitigation: conservative defaults (enforcement_mode=simulate), canary on low-risk fleets, per-tenant overrides.
- Risk: Autoscaler thrash from noisy tension signals. Mitigation: debounce signals, only trigger scale when sustained_deficit > 60s.
- Risk: Complexity in debugging. Mitigation: structured tracing spans, add Console visualization for token balances and headroom heatmaps.
